narrative.overview:
The check result reads like a clinical lab report rendered as a working tool. A night-navy header band carries the instrument (host, port, the teal Check button); below it a white report sheet sits on a pale gray ground, ruled with 1px gray hairlines. The verdict lives in an interpretation box, the tests sit in a result table with their expected values and a flag column, and the certificates are the specimens, folded into rows that open on demand.

Density is the point. This is an Operate-mode surface used mid-incident beside a terminal, so type is compact (15px body on a fixed scale), figures are tabular, and machine identifiers stay in system mono so they copy losslessly. colours are used subtly: black, white and grays carry the page, and Hat Teal appears only where the user acts or focuses. Status colour is quarantined to flags, the validity graph and the paths diagram.

The page follows the OS colour scheme. In dark, the ground and sheet go charcoal and status inks lighten, but the diagram plate stays a light gray so the diagram palette reads true.
keyCharacteristics: Navy header band closed by a 3px yellow rule (bar-edge).
White sheets, 1px hairlines, no shadows; depth is ruled, not lifted.
One family (IBM Plex Sans, self-hosted) on a fixed scale with tabular numerals; system mono for machine identifiers only.
Status as word plus shape (Fail, Warn, Note, Pass with authored 16px icons), tinted red, ochre, slate or green.
Validity drawn to scale on one shared axis with an ink today line.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Hat Teal marks action, selection and focus only. If the accent is telling the user something about the chain, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Red Means Change Rule
rules.body: Red is reserved for findings that need a change. Informational output is slate; nothing decorative is red.

rules.name: The Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Colour lives only in flags, the validity graph and the diagram. Everything else is black, white and gray.

rules.name: The Word-and-Shape Rule
rules.body: Status never relies on colour alone: every status carries its word (Fail, Warn, Note, Pass) and a shape (octagon-x, triangle, circle-i, check), and expired validity bars are hatched.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Sans on the fixed xs to 2xl tokens; no ad hoc sizes, no second display face.

rules.name: The Machine Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono only for strings a user would paste into a terminal or ticket.

rules.name: The Fixed Grid Rule
rules.body: State restyles a row's tint and mark, never the grid. A failing row keeps its columns, widths and position; only its background and flag change.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs separating, draw a hairline or step the tint. Never cast a shadow.

dos: **Do** keep Hat Teal to the primary action, selected tab, focus ring, selection and the header rule.
**Do** pair every status colour with its word and its icon shape; hatch expired bars.
**Do** draw validity to scale on one shared axis with an ink today line.
**Do** use the xs to 2xl type tokens and the 4px spacing scale; keep tabular numerals on.
**Do** keep the diagram plate light in both schemes so the diagram palette stays true.
**Do** meet WCAG 2.2 AA: text at 4.5:1, focus visible, keyboard-operable tabs, fold-outs and copy buttons, reduced motion respected.
donts: **Don't** use the accent as a status colour.
**Don't** use red for anything that does not need a change.
**Don't** let state change a row's grid, column widths or position; restyle tint and mark only.
**Don't** put colour outside the flags, the validity graph and the diagram.
**Don't** add kicker or eyebrow labels above headings.
**Don't** add shadows, soft cards or a second type family.
